# Regression: while a merge is in progress the revealed tree holds the merge
# drivers' output, not yet sealed into the objects (the real seal is deferred to
# pre-commit). A file checkout during the merge fires the post-checkout hook,
# whose file-checkout path used to RevealAll and re-reveal secrets from the stale
# objects - clobbering that unsealed merged plaintext back to ours' content
# (silent data loss that still verified). The hook must skip re-reveal while
# MERGE_HEAD exists. Here a user pokes at theirs' sesam.yml mid-merge with
# `git checkout theirs -- sesam.yml`; the merged secret must survive it.

sesam-repo admin base.txt ours.txt theirs.txt

# Base: a shared secret and bob (dev), so both sides can diverge users (which
# makes sesam.yml differ between the branches).
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt secret.txt
exec sesam add secret.txt --group admin
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret and bob'

# OURS: edit the first line of the secret, extend bob's groups.
exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: first line + bob += ops'

# THEIRS: edit the last line of the secret, kill bob.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec sesam kill --user bob
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: last line + kill bob'

# Merge: secret content-merges cleanly, kill wins over our modify, and sesam.yml
# takes ours via the sesam-ours driver (no conflict). The merge is clean, so
# pre-merge-commit stops the auto-commit (exit 1) with everything resolved.
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file secret.txt; no conflicts'
stderr 'killed on theirs; kill wins'

# The driver put the merged plaintext (both edits) in the revealed file.
grep 'first = OURS' secret.txt
grep 'last = THEIRS' secret.txt

# A file checkout mid-merge (inspecting theirs' config) fires post-checkout. It
# must NOT re-reveal and clobber the unsealed merged secret.
exec git checkout theirs -- sesam.yml
grep 'first = OURS' secret.txt
grep 'last = THEIRS' secret.txt

# Put ours' sesam.yml back (this is the interim policy: take ours) and finalize.
exec git checkout HEAD -- sesam.yml
exec git commit --no-edit
grep 'first = OURS' secret.txt
grep 'last = THEIRS' secret.txt
! grep '^<<<<<<< ' secret.txt

exec sesam verify
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"operation": "user.kill"'
stdout '"operation": "merge"'

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = THEIRS
